notes: All 33 planned steps complete and validated on real hardware (pi3b.local). After Step 33, a spontaneous post-deployment investigation (recorded at the end of tasks.md) found real keypress latency was bad against production content, root-caused via on-hardware CPU profiling to compositeLetterboxed's synchronous CatmullRom upscale of the instant-nav thumbnail (~73% of CPU time, ~1/3 of it this one call). Fixed by making compositeLetterboxed take a scaler parameter: NearestNeighbor for the instant-thumbnail path, CatmullRom retained for the background-decoded full-resolution path. Controlled benchmarks (bench_test.go, kept) confirmed a real ~4.1x win (466ms->113ms/op) and that thumb_width has no meaningful effect on that cost (110-119ms flat across a 12x range, 40-480px) -- informing but not yet deciding the user's separate full-resolution-image-caching idea, which would trade the remaining ~113ms floor for further RSS growth on top of the already-missed 190-200MB baseline. User confirmed the deployed fix felt much better and declined further optimization (a suggested hand-written interface-free NearestNeighbor blit) for now. All board test artifacts cleaned up; one current binary (with the fix) left running against the user's real content at ~jassg/mural/mural.
